questions.explanation: In the vector equation of a line, one vector is the starting point and the other is the direction of travel, so (2, -1) is the direction and (1, 1) is the starting point, reached when t is zero. Negative values are allowed in a direction, and they simply mean the travel has a downward component. Treating the direction as the normal reverses the definition, since a normal must be perpendicular to the line it describes.
questions.hint: One vector is where you start, the other is where you head.

questions.stem: A line is written in vector form as r = (1, 1) + t(2, -1). In that equation, what does the vector (2, -1) represent?
questions.subject: PRECALCULUS

questions.explanation: Every point on the line is (2, -1) + t(3, 4), so solving 2 + 3t = 5 gives t = 1, and the y-value must then be -1 + 4 times 1 = 3, which matches (5, 3). The other pairs each match only one coordinate: (2, 3) needs t = 0 for its x-value, which puts y at -1, and (5, -5) needs t = 1, which puts y at 3. Matching a single coordinate is the trap, because the same t must work for both.
questions.hint: Match both coordinates with one and the same value of t.

questions.stem: A line runs through the point (2, -1) with direction (3, 4). Which ordered pair is a point on that line?
questions.subject: PRECALCULUS

questions.explanation: A direction vector is the end point minus the start point: 5 - 1 = 4 and 6 - 2 = 4, so (4, 4). Any nonzero multiple of (4, 4) would serve as well, and the slope check agrees, since the rise over the run is 4/4 = 1. The sign patterns in the other choices give a slope of -1, which belongs to a different line running the opposite way through the plane.
questions.hint: Subtract the start point from the end point, component by component.

questions.stem: A diagram shows a straight path running from the labeled point (1, 2) to the labeled point (5, 6). Which ordered pair can serve as its direction vector?
questions.subject: PRECALCULUS

questions.explanation: The two sides from the first corner are (5 - 1, 3 - 2) = (4, 1) and (2 - 1, 8 - 2) = (1, 6), and their cross product is 4 times 6 - 1 times 1 = 23, the area of the enclosing parallelogram. A triangle is half of that, so the plot covers 11.5 square units. The shoelace formula confirms it independently, one half of the absolute value of 1 times (3 - 8) + 5 times (8 - 2) + 2 times (2 - 3) being one half of 23. Forgetting the halving reports 23, twice the field.
questions.hint: Build the two side vectors, take their cross product, then halve it.
